translation_notes: Direct mapping of g.query(TEXT) to s{ }: the UNION/FILTER query needs no rewrite beyond the island syntax. Wrote sample1.turtle as the fixture graph (not present in the extracted region) with two reified-statement encodings (explicit rdf:Statement/rdf:predicate, and a node whose own rdf:type is the predicate), plus a plain triple and an incomplete rdf:Statement as non-matching neighbours.

repair.driver: sample1.turtle gains four nodes, each deciding one part of the query: _:untyped (reification triples, no rdf:type), _:otherlink (ex:kind rdf:Statement), _:claim (typed ex:Claim with an rdf:predicate: only the second UNION branch answers) and _:st1dup (same triple as _:st1, for DISTINCT); driver docstring says what each node makes visible. The module-state oracle compares d and res, i.e. what output.json receives.
mutants_killed: anchor `?s rdf:type rdf:Statement` dropped from branch 1
branch 1 rdf:type widened to a variable (`?s ?q rdf:Statement`)
branch 1 object rdf:Statement widened to a variable
branch 1 rdf:predicate widened to a variable
FILTER dropped; branch 2 killed with FILTER(1 = 2); branch 1 killed with FILTER(1 = 2)
branch 2 rdf:type widened; rdf:subject / rdf:object widened
repair.remaining: Nothing on equivalence: the SPARQL text is identical on both sides and every part of it is now decided by a node of the fixture. sample1.turtle stays a fixture invented for the study (the repository has none).

optimization_notes: Both sides: `statements` is inlined into the loop; the two `d[s] = d.get(...)` lines become `d.setdefault(s, {}).setdefault(p, []).append(o)`; `res` is `list(d.values())` after the loop that adds the "uri" key (the inner dicts of d still get it); `json.dump(res, f, indent=2)` replaces `f.write(json.dumps(...))`; `dict()` becomes `{}`; the query text writes rdf:type as `a` and uses `;` (same triples, same order).
optimized.ldpy: s{ } (UNION, FILTER and DISTINCT: not a basic graph pattern) iterated directly on the current graph.
Exception to the symmetry rule, island-only: `@graph as g` replaces the Graph construction, so `import rdflib` goes and `g.parse(...)` stays its own line.
Notation ratio above 1: the query is one string token in Python.
header_optimization_notes: The header is the three provenance comment lines only (the region is the whole module): the two header-variant files are copies of the optimized ones.
